test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 1) Mid-Range Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: What minimum number must be subtracted from 1024 to get the largest 3-digit number which is divisible by 19?
solution:
**Given:**

The number = 1024

**Formula used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

**Calculation:**

Let the subtracted number be X

The largest three-digit number = 999

⇒ 999 = (19 × 52) + 11

The remainder from this number = 11

The difference of the number = 1024 - 999 = 25

The minimum subtracted number X = 25 + 11 = 36

**∴ The required result will be 36.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** For the largest three-digit number the nearest multiple of 19 is 988 and the difference between 1024 and 988 is 36.
